label: Stage Steps — Final Programme Assessment Report
covers: An external evaluator's assessment report about a programme, headerless and in the first-person past tense, signed. Everything in it is a finding about what already happened, so nothing belongs in a grid column. It deliberately carries the trap: sentences that genuinely state the programme's goals, which any item-level test would classify as activities and outcomes. The discriminator has to be the document's authorial stance, not the semantics of a line.

slides.title: Stage Steps — Final Programme Assessment Report, June 2025

columns.heading: ABOUT THIS ASSESSMENT
items: I was commissioned in September to assess the second year of Stage Steps and I visited each partner school twice between October and May.
The goal of the afterschool programme is to give young people a regular creative outlet and a route into performance.
The project is designed to give students a way to express themselves physically and to work together toward something public.

columns.heading: WHAT I OBSERVED
items: Two teaching artists and a coordinator were in post throughout the year, and I found the staffing stable and the sessions well prepared.
Weekly workshops ran in all four schools, although the Thursday group lost four weeks in February when the hall was double-booked.
At the spring performances you could see that the students had learned to hold an audience, to take a cue from one another, and to recover when something went wrong.

columns.heading: WHAT THE SURVEYS SHOWED
items: Sixty-one young people returned the end-of-year survey and forty-eight of them said they would take part again.
Teachers reported that students enjoy the classes, which give them the opportunity to express themselves physically.
Attendance averaged seventy-one per cent, which I would treat with caution because two schools counted it differently.

columns.heading: RECOMMENDATIONS
items: Agree a single definition of attendance across all four schools before the next year begins.
Commission an independent assessment of the confidence claim, which this report cannot substantiate.
Signed: A. Merrow, independent evaluator, June 2025.
